subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which base does the binary number system use?
options: Base 2
Base 8
Base 10
Base 16
questions.explain: Binary is a base-2 system using only the digits 0 and 1.

questions.q: How many different digit symbols are used in the hexadecimal number system?
questions.explain: Hexadecimal is base 16, using 0-9 and then A-F to represent the values 10-15.

questions.q: How many bits are there in a nibble?
questions.explain: A nibble is 4 bits, which is half of a byte.

questions.q: How many bits make up one byte?
questions.explain: A byte consists of 8 bits.

questions.q: According to the AQA specification, how many bytes are there in one kilobyte?
questions.explain: AQA uses powers of ten, so 1 kilobyte equals 1000 bytes.

questions.q: How many bits are used to represent a single character in standard 7-bit ASCII?
questions.explain: Standard ASCII uses 7 bits per character, allowing 128 different characters.

questions.q: What is the sample rate when recording sound?
options: The number of samples taken per second
The number of bits used to store each sample
The total length of the recording in seconds
The loudness of the sound wave
questions.explain: Sample rate is how many times per second the amplitude of the analogue signal is measured, usually given in hertz.

questions.q: Which compression technique builds a binary tree based on the frequency of characters in the data?
options: Huffman coding
Run-length encoding
Lossy compression
Analogue-to-digital conversion
questions.explain: Huffman coding assigns shorter binary codes to more frequent characters using a frequency-based tree.

questions.q: Why do programmers often prefer to use hexadecimal rather than binary?
options: Hexadecimal represents large binary values using fewer, more manageable digits
Hexadecimal can store larger numbers than binary can
Hexadecimal is the only base a computer can process directly
Hexadecimal removes the need to store any data in binary
questions.explain: Each hex digit maps to 4 binary bits, so long binary strings become shorter and easier to read and less error-prone.

questions.q: Which sequence lists units of storage from smallest to largest?
options: Bit, nibble, byte, kilobyte, megabyte
Byte, bit, nibble, megabyte, kilobyte
Nibble, bit, byte, megabyte, kilobyte
Bit, byte, nibble, kilobyte, megabyte
questions.explain: The order increases as bit (1), nibble (4 bits), byte (8 bits), kilobyte (1000 bytes) then megabyte.

questions.q: When does an overflow error occur during binary addition?
options: When the result is too large to fit in the available number of bits
When two binary numbers have different lengths
When a binary number contains a decimal point
When the answer contains more zeros than ones
questions.explain: Overflow happens when a calculation produces a result that needs more bits than are available to store it.

questions.q: What is the effect of performing a single left binary shift on an unsigned binary number?
options: It multiplies the number by 2
It divides the number by 2
It adds 1 to the number
It leaves the number unchanged
questions.explain: Each left shift moves every bit one place higher in value, multiplying the number by 2.

questions.q: An image has a colour depth of 4 bits per pixel. How many different colours can each pixel represent?
questions.explain: The number of colours equals 2 to the power of the colour depth, and 2^4 = 16.

questions.q: What is the effect of increasing the sample rate when recording a sound?
options: Higher sound quality but a larger file size
Lower sound quality but a smaller file size
Higher sound quality with no change in file size
No change to sound quality but a larger file size
questions.explain: More samples per second capture the wave more accurately, improving quality but increasing the amount of data stored.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes lossless compression?
options: The original data can be reconstructed exactly from the compressed file
Some data is permanently removed to reduce the file size
It can only be used on sound files
It always produces smaller files than lossy compression
questions.explain: Lossless compression reduces file size while allowing the exact original data to be restored.

questions.q: How does run-length encoding (RLE) reduce the size of a file?
options: By replacing sequences of repeated values with a single value and a count
By deleting every second bit in the file
By converting the file to hexadecimal
By rounding colour values to the nearest whole number
questions.explain: RLE stores a repeated run as one value plus the number of times it repeats, saving space when data contains long runs.

questions.q: What is the 8-bit binary number 00101101 in denary?
questions.explain: The set bits have values 32 + 8 + 4 + 1, which sum to 45.

questions.q: What is the result of adding the 8-bit binary numbers 00110101 and 00010011?
questions.explain: 00110101 is 53 and 00010011 is 19; their sum 72 is 01001000 in binary.

questions.q: What is the binary number 11101010 written in hexadecimal?
options: AE
EA
EB
FA
questions.explain: Splitting into nibbles gives 1110 (E) and 1010 (A), so the value is EA.

questions.q: An image is 100 pixels wide by 50 pixels high with a colour depth of 3 bits. What is its file size in bits, ignoring metadata?
questions.explain: File size equals width x height x colour depth, so 100 x 50 x 3 = 15000 bits.

specSource: AQA GCSE Computer Science (8525) specification; Fundamentals Of Data Representation
